latest_nl_proof:
Let r_k denote the least residue of ak modulo n, for 1 <= k <= n-1. We must show that after sorting the multiset {r_1, ..., r_{n-1}} in nonincreasing order, the j-th term u_j satisfies u_j <= n-j.

If a = 0, then every r_k = 0, so u_j = 0 for all j. Since n-j >= 1 for 1 <= j <= n-1, the inequality holds.

Now assume a > 0. Write n = dm, where d = gcd(a,n), and write a = da_0. Then gcd(a_0,m) = 1.

Fix s with 1 <= s <= m-1 and q with 0 <= q <= d-1, and set k = qm + s. Then 1 <= k <= n-1, and
ak = d a_0(qm+s) = d(a_0 q m + a_0 s) ≡ d(a_0 s) (mod dm = n).
Let ρ_s be the least residue of a_0 s modulo m. Then ρ_s lies in {1, ..., m-1} because gcd(a_0,m) = 1, and the least residue of ak modulo n is exactly dρ_s.

As s runs through 1, ..., m-1, the residues ρ_s run through 1, ..., m-1 exactly once, because multiplication by a_0 is a permutation of the nonzero residue classes modulo m. Therefore, among the residues r_1, ..., r_{n-1}, each value d, 2d, ..., (m-1)d occurs exactly d times.

What about 0? If k is a positive multiple of m, say k = qm with 1 <= q <= d-1, then ak = da_0(qm) is divisible by n = dm, so r_k = 0. There are exactly d-1 such k. Hence the multiset of residues consists of:
- d copies of each value d, 2d, ..., (m-1)d;
- d-1 copies of 0.

After sorting in nonincreasing order, the list is therefore
u_1 = ... = u_d = n-d,
u_{d+1} = ... = u_{2d} = n-2d,
...
u_{(m-1)d+1} = ... = u_{n-1} = 0.
Equivalently, for each i = 1, ..., m-1, we have u_j = n-id whenever (i-1)d < j <= id, and for j > (m-1)d we have u_j = 0.

Now let j be any integer with 1 <= j <= n-1. If j <= (m-1)d, choose i with (i-1)d < j <= id. Then u_j = n-id <= n-j, since j <= id. If j > (m-1)d, then u_j = 0 <= n-j. Thus in all cases u_j <= n-j.

This proves the lemma.
role_in_parent: Supply the pointwise majorization u_j <= n-j for the sorted residue list.
statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, let d = gcd(a,n) and m = n/d. Let u_1 >= u_2 >= ... >= u_{n-1} be the least residues Res_n(a,1), ..., Res_n(a,n-1) arranged in nonincreasing order. Then u_j <= n-j for every integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1.

domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
a is an integer with 0 <= a <= n-1
d is defined as gcd(a,n) and is treated as a positive integer
m is defined as n/d and is therefore an integer
Res_n(a,k) is defined for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1
each least residue Res_n(a,k) is an integer in the standard least-residue range (typically 0 through n-1)
the sequence u_1 through u_{n-1} is arranged so that u_1 >= u_2 >= ... >= u_{n-1}
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1, for all integers a with 0 <= a <= n-1: define d = gcd(a,n) and m = n/d. Consider the multiset of least residues of a*k modulo n for k = 1,...,n-1, and sort them in nonincreasing order to obtain u_1,...,u_{n-1}. Then for every integer j with 1 <= j <= n-1, the inequality u_j <= n - j holds.

variables.name: j
variables.role: index in the sorted residue list

variables.name: u_j
variables.role: j-th element of the multiset of least residues Res_n(a,1) through Res_n(a,n-1), sorted in nonincreasing order

witness_dependencies: d depends on n and a via d = gcd(a,n)
m depends on n and d via m = n/d
the multiset being sorted that defines u_1 through u_{n-1} depends on n and a via the values Res_n(a,k) for k from 1 to n-1
u_j depends on n, a, and the sorting (nonincreasing order) of those residue values
